reason: A common cross-family primary constraint envelope cannot be frozen for the scalar and axial simplified classes without additional UV/thermal-history/branching-ratio/hadronic assumptions. Laboratory constraints can be recorded under explicit conventions, but astrophysical/cosmological/collider limits are not universally transportable to the independent-coupling benchmark planes frozen in 0070a.

vector.note: Single gauge coupling fixes relative neutrino/electron/quark B-L charges; do not identify with phenomenological universal-vector product conventions.

scalar.note: External constraints often assume equal couplings, Higgs-portal/Yukawa relations, Majorana/LNV structure, right-handed-neutrino thermalization, or specific scalar nucleon form factors.

axial.note: Collider/cosmology/stellar mappings depend on anomaly-cancellation and longitudinal-mode UV completion; nucleon mapping depends on spin fractions and quark-coupling pattern.

primary_authority.citation: V. De Romeri, D. K. Papoulias, C. A. Ternes, JCAP 05 (2025) 012
primary_authority.role: Primary reanalysis of XENONnT/PandaX-4T CEvNS and electron-recoil data for scalar, vector, B-L and axial light mediators; explicit coupling convention and model-dependence audit.
facts_used: Defines effective Lorentz structures and light-mediator couplings.
Assumes equal mediator coupling strengths to neutrinos, quarks and charged leptons in the universal benchmark, with g_a=sqrt(g_nu_a g_q_a)=sqrt(g_nu_a g_l_a).
Scalar/vector nuclear coefficients require hadronic/nuclear conventions.
Axial/tensor nuclear response is spin dependent.
States astrophysical/cosmological regions are strongly model-dependent and require tailored analyses.
Notes axial limits change materially when quark and lepton couplings are allowed to differ.

primary_authority.citation: L. J. Flores et al., Phys. Rev. D 113, 095019 (2026)
primary_authority.role: Primary analysis showing that multiple generalized-neutrino-interaction parametrizations require explicit translations before comparing bounds.
facts_used: Different common GNI parametrizations are not identical by inspection and require an explicit relation.
Scalar/vector/tensor constraints from CEvNS and DIS depend on the chosen normalization.

laboratory_neutrino_scattering_CEvNS.note: JCAP 05 (2025) 012 provides a single internally consistent universal-coupling comparison and B-L benchmark, but this does not universalize independent-coupling scalar/axial models.

collider_fixed_target.note: Visible/invisible decay searches depend on mediator branching ratios and additional couplings; no universal mapping to independent g_nu*g_f planes.

stellar_supernova.note: Production, free streaming and trapping depend on the complete coupling pattern and medium interactions.

cosmology_BBN_CMB_free_streaming.note: Depends on thermal history, mediator population, neutrino chirality/extra states and decay channels.

fifth_force_equivalence_principle.note: Directly constrains ordinary-matter charges/couplings; conversion to a neutrino-matter product requires a relation between matter and neutrino couplings. B-L is a suitable separately gauge-complete benchmark.

scientific_decision.next_gate: Freeze a dedicated gauge-complete U(1)_{B-L} primary constraint ledger in (m_V,g_BL) only, including laboratory, collider/fixed-target, stellar/SN, cosmological and fifth-force families without recasting incompatible universal-product models.
